newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids steady to lower, HSFO weak.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids steady to lower, HSFO weak.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices were steady to lower again Thursday in lackluster trade, with sentiment still bearish as ample supplies, mild weather and cheap natgas continued to weigh on the complex, sources said.
"There's a lot of fear in the market about too much supply. Everyone's got barrels and no one needs them," said one cash trader, noting U.S. Gulf high sulphur seemed under the most pressure.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent eased slightly to the $16.25 a barrel area, with March one percent paper also quoted modestly lower in the high-$15s, traders said.
Traders said recently cheaper city gate gas prices have drawn some East Coast utilities away from resid.
NYH 0.3 percent low pour and high pour again notionally held steady at $19.25 and $17.25-50, respectively.
NYH high sulphurs were lower, with three percent off 25-50 cents to about $14.50, traders said.

At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was stable at $14.75-15.00. But USG three percent skidded 25-50 cents to $12.25 or lower amid a growing tide of offers and weaker bunker prices. At least three majors were seen offering USG high sulphur barrels, traders said.
A trader said 60,000 barrels of prompt 3.2 percent sold at $11.75 (delivered Houston).

March New York city gate gas prices again held steady Thursday at about the $2.15/mmBtu, or about $13.55 a barrel equivalent. March gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, also was unchanged at about $1.80/mmBtu, or $11.34 a barrel equivalent.
